name: Sprocket
text:
Adopt the rolling 30-day usage-weighted decay metric. It catches silent failures better than a fixed 7-day window while still pruning stale high-usage prompts faster than a flat 30-day rule. The trade-off is slightly slower responsiveness to fresh regressions, but the stability gain from catching silent failures outweighs that risk.

name: Gauge
text: The rolling 30-day usage-weighted decay still misses silent failures in low-usage prompts—weighting by usage just hides the problem. A better alternative: pair a 7-day decay for top 20% prompts with a 90-day *static* decay for the rest, then measure silent failure rates in the long tail. Settle it by running a 30-day A/B test tracking both fresh regression detection *and* silent failure rates across usage tiers.
